title: Lovely Northern Suet Pudding Spot
description: A hearty, comforting British dish featuring a crumbly suet pudding cake spot, served with a side of homemade custard. Traditionally served for breakfast or as a snack.

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.notes: Scalded milk is ideal for this recipe

ingredients.name: Soda water
ingredients.notes: To make the suet pudding lighter

instructions: Preheat the oven to 1804C (350F) and grease a 1-pint pudding basin.
Mix together the flour, suet, sugar, and baking powder in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs and milk.
Add the salt, raisins, and currants to the flour mixture and stir to combine.
Pour in the wet ingredients and mix until just combined.
Turn the mixture into the prepared pudding basin and pour in the soda water.
Cover the pudding with parchment paper or a clean tea towel and tie with kitchen string.
Place the pudding in a large saucepan and add enough boiling water to come halfway up the pudding basin.
Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cover the saucepan with a lid.
Steam the pudding for 2 hours, topping up the water as needed.
Remove the pudding from the saucepan and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Invert the pudding onto a serving plate and serve with homemade custard.
To make the custard, combine 200g of milk with 2 egg yolks and 25g of sugar in a saucepan. Cook over a low heat, stirring constantly, until the custard thickens.
Remove the custard from the heat and strain it into a clean bowl. Let it cool to room temperature before serving.
